title: [YouPass Collect] - Average hours to produce cars in the US
prompt: The graph below shows the average time spent by four car manufacturers to produce vehicles at their US factories. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the average time required to manufacture automobiles at US factories by four major car companies over an 8-year period from 1998 to 2005.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, all manufacturers needed less time to produce cars over the period shown, with General Motors showing the most notable improvement in its production time. In addition, Honda consistently maintained the lowest duration for the most part of the period.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the two American manufacturers, in 1998, General Motors took the longest time of 32 hours to produce a car, about 4 hours more than Ford. The former company then saw a steady decline in its figures, ultimately falling to 22 hours by 2005. Meanwhile, the number of hours to make Ford cars peaked at 31 hours in 2001, before reducing by a third, plunging to only 21 hours by the end of the timeframe.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining companies, in 1998, both Toyota and Honda required approximately 22 hours per vehicle, by far the fastest turnaround. Thereafter, Toyota's production time showed fluctuations between 22 and 24 hours, followed by a significant decrease in the last 2 years, ending up at just 20 hours in 2005. Likewise, despite a drop by 2 hours by 1999, Honda’s numbers picked up to reach a high of 24 hours in 2002, before falling back to a similar level of 20 hours by the final year.
